chunks: And Muhammad ibn Adam narrated from al-Rida (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who says to his slave girl, 'I have freed you, and I have made your dowry your freedom,' he said: 'The manumission is valid, and the matter is up to her; if she wishes, she may marry herself to him, and if she wishes, she may not. If she marries herself to him, I would like him to give her something.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a master frees his slave girl and makes her dowry her freedom?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida clarifies that manumission with mahr as freedom is legally valid, granting the freed slave girl full autonomy to accept or reject marriage to her former master. This ruling highlights the transition from servitude to independent legal personhood, where her consent is paramount. The recommendation for the master to provide a gift upon marriage underscores the ethical continuity of care and respect in the master-slave relationship within Shia jurisprudence.
